# Synthetic model acceptance fixtures

These small Unity 2022.3, format-22 player SerializedFiles are generated by
`tests/models.rs`. They contain no proprietary game data or executable code.
Fixture builders derive under MIT from the pinned `unity-rs` test builders,
copyright (c) 2016 Radu, (c) 2016–2022 Perfare, and (c) 2021–2025 aelurum.

- `triangle.assets`: one GameObject/Transform/MeshFilter/MeshRenderer, triangle,
  material, 1×1 texture and legacy animation. The transform translates by (2,3,4).
- `static-world.assets`: two differently transformed owners share a six-vertex
  mesh. Each renderer selects one triangle/submesh and one separate material.
  A null batch root means the stored geometry is already in world coordinates.
- `static-root.assets`: the same pair, with an independently rooted batch
  transform at (100,10,5), Z rotation 90°, scale (2,3,4). The owner transforms
  differ, including negative/nonuniform scale. Source normals and red/blue
  vertex colors verify actual channel remapping. The unrelated root remains
  outside either selected owner's subtree.

Regenerate using `ASSETSTUDIO_MODEL_TEST_OUT` when running the model integration
tests and copy the corresponding generated `.assets` files. The fixtures encode
the actual parser layouts but are synthetic, not a real-game compatibility
oracle. Independent FBX import checks are recorded separately.

The root-space reconstruction follows Unity's documented static-batching model:
[static batching](https://docs.unity3d.com/cn/2023.1/Manual/static-batching.html),
[root movement](https://docs.unity3d.com/ja/2023.2/ScriptReference/StaticBatchingUtility.Combine.html)
and the distinction between
[renderer and Transform matrices](https://docs.unity3d.com/ja/6000.0/ScriptReference/Renderer-localToWorldMatrix.html).
The implementation uses original Rust matrix/subset code; no Unity reference
source implementation is copied into the application.
